title.narrative: Support to PRSP process and poverty analysis

description.narrative: Objective The purpose of the grant is to finance activities identified by the Government of Guineacomma through the PRS Committeecomma as critical to the achievement of the Poverty Reduction Strategy. The IDF grant will support the process by which the Poverty Reduction Strategy is elaborated and strengthen the in-country data collection and analytical capacity that will provide the poverty relevant information and analysis necessary to (i) provide an analysis of poverty characteristics and determinants; (ii) assist policy-makers in monitoring levels and trends of povertycomma design strategiescomma policies and programs; (iii) implement the latter with the highest impact on poverty reduction; and (iv) ensure adequate and timely monitoring and evaluation of the activities as described in the Interim PRSP. Components The first two activities would establish a permanent institutional mechanism to produce the PRSP and the following progress reportscomma including the establishment of an Observatory for Poverty Reduction. The other activities will aim to (i) set up a poverty monitoring system; (ii) help organize and disseminate the existing datacomma and (iii) give to decision makers a tool (poverty map) to target the poverty reduction related activities. Component 1: Institutionalization of PRSP process To establish a permanent institutional mechanism for the PRS Committee to designcomma monitor the implementationcomma evaluate the poverty reduction strategycomma and produce the PRSP and the following Progress Reports. This activity will include (i) the proposal of institutional mechanisms for the PRSP process; (ii) a study tour for the PRS Committee to review what has been done in other African countries (Tunisia and Egypt Tunisia and Egypt have been selected because both countries have established successful social funds as key instrument to reduce poverty. ) and discuss targeted PRSP activitiescomma i.e. Social Funds ; (iii) three workshops/training with governmentcomma civil societycomma local governmentscomma NGOscomma and donors will allow the PRS Committee to share and discuss the PRSP process; first workshop: sharing and discussing the sectoral strategies; second workshop: establishing priorities and tradeoffs; and third workshop: finalizing the PRSP. Three fourths of the attendance will come from the regions; and (iv) the dissemination of documents and information to the PRSP stakeholderscomma and the public on the poverty reduction strategy. Component 2: Establishment of an Observatory of Poverty Reduction To establish a poverty analysis center (Observatory of Poverty Reduction) that will (i) analyze poverty trends and determinants; (ii) monitor the implementation of poverty strategiescomma policiescomma programs and projects including the selection of relevant indicators; and (iii) evaluate their impact on poverty reduction. The Observatory will publish an annual report on Poverty in Guinea. This activity will include: (i) the proposal of the Observatory including legal textscomma staffingcomma compositioncomma managementcomma action plancomma outputscomma budgetcomma and time table; (ii) a study tour in neighboring countries (Malicomma Benin) to review the experiences of existing Observatoriescomma and (iii) workshop with the staff and users of the Observatory to discuss the proposalcomma and finalize its different elements. commacommacommacomma Component 3: Definition and establishment of an Integrated Statistical Information System for Poverty Reduction To create an Integrated Statistical Information System for Poverty Reduction (ISISPR) that produces quantitative and qualitative informationcomma at (i) nationalcomma regional and community levelcomma for sectoral and intersectoral issuescomma and (ii) at household and individual levels. The ISISPR will include the existing statistical services from the sectoral ministers. This activity will include (i) the design of the overall system including statistics productioncomma information flowscomma and expected outputs; and (ii) two workshops with Governmentcomma civil society and donors participation. The first workshop will discuss the system featurescomma and the selection of performance indicatorscomma and the second workshop will review the first year production of the system. Component 4: Data Bankcomma Documentationcomma Dissemination This component will allow the documentation of existing data and the organization in a data bank (à la Africa Household Survey Data Bank)comma as well as the production of a CDROM and the establishment of three web sites to disseminate the data.§ §Poverty Data Bank : To establish at the National Statistical Department (DNS) a data bank where survey primary data and metadata will be storedcomma and made readily available to users. The activity includes (i) the establishment of the data bank software; (ii) the training of DNS staff; (iii) the gathering of data and the scanning of the documentation; and (iv) a workshop to present the data bank and to define the role of data producers and users. §Poverty CDROM : a preparation and dissemination of a CD-ROM containing all existing reports related to poverty to date. This stock taking exercise would mainly involve all statistics producers. The CDROM production will build on the Data Bank results. This activity includes (i) the design of the CDROM structure and the search tool; (ii) the training of DNS staff; (iii) the gathering of the documentationcomma and the scanning of the documents selectedcomma and (iv) the dissemination of the CDROM. Web sites : To develop three web sites (interlinked)comma one for the PRS Committeecomma one for the National Statistical Departmentcomma and one for the Observatory. This activity includes (i) the design and installation of the three web sites; (ii) the training of local staff to maintain it; (ii) the gathering and scanning of the documentation to be put on the web sites; and (iv) the review and fine tuning of the web sites one year after their installation. Component 5: Poverty map To develop the capacity of the DNS and other statistical personnel to elaborate and regularly update poverty maps based on 15 to 20 indicatorscomma previously developed by international consultants. These poverty maps would be tailored to the specific needs (especially targeting) of various policy makers as they elaborate their Poverty Reduction Strategy and would allow wide dissemination and discussion within the country and with development partners. This activity includes (i) the review and update of the system; (ii) the training of poverty map users; (ii) the collection and processing of new data; and (iii) a workshop to discuss the features of the poverty map and disseminate the results.
